title: Preparation for Calculus
intro: Build the language of calculus with graphs, functions and models fitted to data. Compare linear, quadratic and periodic models using residuals and domain knowledge.
prerequisites: Basic algebra and coordinate geometry. Use the study-plan trigonometry reference as needed.

sectionTitles.P.2: Linear Models and Rates of Change

title: Limits and Their Properties
intro: Understand nearby behavior, one-sided limits, continuity and unbounded behavior before defining a derivative.
prerequisites: Preparation: functions, domains and algebraic simplification.

title: Differentiation
intro: Build derivatives from limits, then calculate rates using rules, implicit relations and time-dependent geometry.

sectionTitles.2.1: The Derivative and the Tangent Line Problem
sectionTitles.2.2: Basic Differentiation Rules and Rates of Change
sectionTitles.2.3: The Product and Quotient Rules and Higher-Order Derivatives

title: Applications of Differentiation
intro: Use derivatives to justify graph shape, extrema, approximations and numerical roots, then apply marginal analysis to business and economics.
prerequisites: Chapter 2: derivative rules and tangent lines.

sectionTitles.3.2: Rolle’s Theorem and the Mean Value Theorem
sectionTitles.3.3: Increasing and Decreasing Functions and the First Derivative Test
sectionTitles.3.4: Concavity and the Second Derivative Test

title: Integration
intro: Build integration from finite sums, connect accumulation to antiderivatives, and compare numerical integration rules.
prerequisites: Chapters 1–3: limits, derivatives and function behavior.

title: Logarithmic, Exponential, and Other Transcendental Functions
intro: Extend calculus to logarithms, exponentials, inverses and hyperbolic functions. Solve growth/decay and separable differential equations in their sixth-edition locations.
prerequisites: Chapters 2 and 4: chain rule, antiderivatives and substitution.

sectionTitles.5.1: The Natural Logarithmic Function and Differentiation
sectionTitles.5.2: The Natural Logarithmic Function and Integration
sectionTitles.5.5: Bases Other than e and Applications

title: Applications of Integration
intro: Turn geometry and physical accumulation into integrals for area, volume, length, work, mass and fluid force.
prerequisites: Chapters 4–5: definite integrals and transcendental functions.

sectionTitles.6.1: Area of a Region Between Two Curves
sectionTitles.6.4: Arc Length and Surfaces of Revolution
sectionTitles.6.6: Moments, Centers of Mass, and Centroids

title: Integration Techniques, L’Hôpital’s Rule, and Improper Integrals
intro: Choose integration techniques, use L’Hôpital’s rule under its hypotheses, and handle infinite intervals and singularities through limits.
prerequisites: Chapters 4–5: basic antiderivatives, substitution, logarithms and trigonometry.

sectionTitles.7.6: Integration by Tables and Other Integration Techniques

title: Infinite Series
intro: Study convergence, error control, power series and representation by Taylor and Maclaurin series.
prerequisites: Chapters 1–5 and 7: limits, derivatives, integration and improper integrals.

sectionTitles.8.9: Representation of Functions by Power Series

title: Conics, Parametric Equations, and Polar Coordinates
intro: Use conics and new curve coordinates to calculate slopes, area, length and orbital geometry.
prerequisites: Chapters 2, 4–5 and 6–7: differentiation, integration and trigonometry.

sectionTitles.9.5: Area and Arc Length in Polar Coordinates
sectionTitles.9.6: Polar Equations of Conics and Kepler’s Laws
